To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TFs involved in drought response in plants may be used for developing drought tolerant crops.
TFs involved in drought response have been described, and their possible use for development of drought resistant cultivars discussed.
TFs involved in drought responses in plants are important in developing drought tolerant wheat cultivars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of transcription factors (and their target genes) involved in the response to drought stress in wheat, and their use to improve the drought tolerance of the crop.
the identification of genes involved in drought and salt tolerance in plants, and the use of this knowledge for developing drought and salt tolerant cultivars of cereals and other important crops.
the development and application of molecular markers for wheat improvement, and the identification of molecular mechanisms underlying the drought tolerance of wheat cultivars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of TFs in drought tolerance has been established beyond doubt.
TFs and their regulons are involved in drought tolerance, and may be useful for developing drought tolerant varieties of wheat, rice, and other crops in the near future.
the TFs involved in drought stress tolerance in wheat have been identified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TFs involved in drought responses are a good source of genes for improving the tolerance to drought stress in wheat and other cereals.
TF genes and the regulons they control are the key to drought tolerance, and that these genes may be exploited to develop drought tolerant cultivars.
the TFs belonging to AP2/EREBPs, bZips, MYBs/MYCs, NACs and WRKYS are the most important TFs involved in drought response and tolerance in plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although TFs involved in response to abiotic stresses in plants have been studied for quite some time now, there are still many aspects of their function and the networks they are involved in that remain to be understood.

TF genes can be used for development of drought-tolerant cultivars in wheat and other crops.
